title: Appearance — the theme editor and the grouping

steps.page: The theme editor (the pencil on your own themes)
steps.intro: The pencil appears only on themes you built yourself. Most of what it opens repeats Additional customizations; three things are only there.

steps.path: Settings → Appearance → the pencil on a theme you built
steps.headline: What happens to the separate theme editor?
steps.today: The pencil opens "Edit: <theme name>": accent colour, roundness, particles, glass sliders, terminal sliders and Publish to Marketplace. Roundness and every glass and terminal slider also live in Additional customizations, where they apply to every theme.
steps.problem: Two places change the same things, and when Additional customizations is set, the editor's sliders go grey with a long note explaining why. You said you want this menu gone.
steps.proposal: Remove it, and move the few things only it has to the places in the next two questions.

options.label: Remove it
pros: One place for every look setting.
No greyed-out sliders, no clashing values.
The theme cards lose the pencil, so they're simpler.
cons: Changing your own theme's built-in roundness or glass now means asking Claude (the Additional customizations versions still work).

options.label: Keep a slim one
options.summary: The pencil stays on your own themes, but opens only accent colour, particles and Publish.
cons: Still a second, separate menu, which is what you didn't like.

steps.headline: If the editor goes, which of its settings should move into Additional customizations?
steps.today: Accent colour (the colour of buttons and highlights) and particles (falling snow, sparkles and so on) can only be changed in the editor, and only on themes you built.
steps.problem: Without the editor, there would be no hand control for them at all.
steps.proposal: Moved settings would start on Auto (the theme's own choice) and work on every theme, like the others there. Pick none and they're changed by asking Claude.

options.label: Particles
pros: Turn snow or sparkles on or off on any theme.
A short row of pictures, like Message bubbles.
cons: One more row in the panel.

options.label: Accent colour
pros: Pick your favourite colour on any theme.
cons: On themes someone else designed, a picked colour can clash or make button text hard to read.
A colour picker is a bigger, fiddlier control than the tile rows around it.

options.label: Neither
pros: The panel stays the size it is.
cons: Changing them means asking Claude to edit your theme.

steps.path: Settings → Appearance → a theme you built
steps.headline: Where should Publish to Marketplace be once the editor is gone?
steps.today: Publish sits at the bottom of the editor. It is also the Share button on the theme's page in Your library.
steps.problem: If the editor goes, Publish is only in Your library, which is easy to miss from Appearance.

options.label: Share icon on the card
options.summary: Your own themes show a small share icon where the pencil was; it opens the same publish screen.
pros: Visible right where you see your theme.
Only on themes you made, so it says "this one is yours".
cons: One more small icon on those cards, beside the star.

options.label: Library only
pros: Theme cards stay as clean as the rest.
cons: You'd have to know to look in Your library.

steps.intro: Today: Themes, then Layout with a folded Additional customizations row (message bubbles, roundness, glass), then Effects & chat (Reduce visual effects, Message timestamps).

steps.headline: How should the rest of the screen, below Themes, be grouped?
steps.today: Layout's four tiles sit bare, then one folded row called "Additional customizations" hides bubbles, roundness and glass. Below it, "Effects & chat" mixes an accessibility switch with a chat setting.
steps.problem: "Additional customizations" doesn't say what's in it, the fold hides most settings, and the groups don't match what's inside them. You asked to rearrange and regroup this.
steps.proposal: Three ways to sort the same settings. In each, every group is a small label over a card, per the guide.

options.label: Named groups, nothing folded
options.summary: Themes · Window (layout tiles, roundness) · Chat (message bubbles, timestamps) · Glass & effects (glass, Fine-tune, particles if moved, Reduce visual effects).
pros: Every setting visible, under a label that says what it is.
cons: A longer screen: about two screens of scrolling instead of one and a bit.

options.label: Same groups, folded
options.summary: The same four groups, but Window, Chat and Glass & effects each open and close like today's row.
pros: Short screen; you open only what you need.
cons: Settings stay hidden until you open them.

options.label: A Customize page
options.summary: Appearance shows Themes and Layout only; one "Customize" row opens a page with Chat and Glass & effects.
pros: The main screen is very short.
Works like Fine-tune glass already does.
cons: Every tweak is one more click and a page change away.
